findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional recursive BST deletion: ordering restricts the search to one branch, zero- and one-child targets return their surviving child directly, and a two-child target is replaced by the minimum value from its right subtree before that successor is removed. It is clear, compact, and already expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 450 and a runnable Python tree contract. The app-local source defines the required minimal TreeNode equivalent, converts the level-order input to links, invokes the reviewed deletion, and serializes the returned root back to the app representation.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064848982. Its comparisons, one-branch recursion, direct child returns, right-subtree minimum scan, successor-value copy, and recursive successor deletion match the protected app-local algorithm and data flow exactly; the only structural differences are the local model and app adapter.

The 63-, 255-, and 511-node balanced-tree tiers span more than 8x and require deletion after exercising the complete app adapter. The current source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.00x the reference runtime. A correct control that first clones the BST through repeated preorder insertion passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 154.32x, distinguishing its slower construction growth.

The Approach now corresponds exactly to the protected target: it derives the ordered search, explains both direct-child cases and successor replacement, and separates the native O(h) deletion from the standalone adapter's O(n) full-tree conversions. Its alternatives identify their concrete tradeoffs and all material deletion boundaries.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves both deletion stages, all three exact example facts and explanation statuses, both valid first-example outcomes, all five constraints, the O(height of tree) follow-up, and the two source tree visuals through independently authored accessible Mermaid diagrams.
